evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry distinguishes Xu Shen’s pregnancy explanation for 包 from wrapping/enclosing uses cited from transmitted texts, including the Shijing line 白茅包之. It lists these separately and supplies no evidence that the wrapping sense historically developed from the pregnancy sense. This supports removing the proposed pregnancy-to-wrap development edge; it does not establish that the two senses are historically unrelated.
evidence.title: [A00408] 包 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Institute of History and Philology, Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The character page describes the Shuowen account as pregnancy, with the middle shape interpreted as an unformed child. Its visible text presents that traditional account but does not supply a dated semantic chain to the transmitted wrapping use.
evidence.title: 漢字「包」：字形演變

evidence.text: The search result surfaced a page reproducing historical commentary on 包, but opening the page returned HTTP 403. Its contents are not used as verified evidence.

search_audit.query: 包 字 说文 妊 白茅包之 语义 来源
search_audit.outcome: Search returned a Ministry dictionary entry and secondary materials. The Ministry entry was opened; it separately records the Shuowen pregnancy interpretation and transmitted wrapping examples, without establishing a semantic transition.

search_audit.query: site:dict.variants.moe.edu.tw/dictView.jsp 包 妊 白茅包之
search_audit.outcome: Opened the Ministry entry and inspected its explanation and senses. It gives the pregnancy interpretation, quotes 白茅包之 under containing/wrapping, and lists later senses, but does not date their development.

search_audit.query: 包 字源 妊 包裹 语义演变
search_audit.outcome: Opened the Academia Sinica page; its displayed text repeats the pregnancy interpretation but provides no semantic chronology. Chinese Text Project returned HTTP 403 and the dictionary PDF exceeded the browser content limit. Neither failed page is used as evidence.

gaps: The pregnancy gloss is a historical Shuowen interpretation; the inspected sources do not establish that wrapping developed from it, nor do they establish that the senses are unrelated. The pregnancy-to-wrap development edge should be removed or replaced with an unresolved relationship.
The Ministry entry quotes the transmitted Shijing wrapping example but does not establish the date of its written witness or a dated chronology for subsequent senses.
